title: Suggestions beta — risk levels (working draft)
text:
Suggestions beta — risk levels (working draft)

Context / why this doc exists
- We need a simple, consistent “risk level” for the Optimization suggestions beta (batching + caching only) shown in the Console Suggestions list + details drawer.
- Goal: help a user decide “do I try this?” without overpromising; risk should be conservative and paired with explicit guardrails and assumptions.
- IMPORTANT: “risk” here is NOT security/privacy risk. It’s operational risk: performance SLO impact + reliability / error-rate impact, plus (secondary) output stability risk if the recommendation changes request execution patterns.
- This is an iterative draft. We expect to tune thresholds after dogfood + private beta.

Audience
- Primary: ML/platform engineers and app owners responsible for latency SLOs.
- Secondary: engineering managers / stakeholders who will ask “why is this labeled High?”

Beta scope constraints
- Suggestions types in scope: batching adjustments; caching enablement/tuning (prefix/KV/prompt cache settings depending on model/runtime).
- Out of scope: quantization recommendations and any automatic application.
- Risk label must be explainable with 2–4 bullets; avoid opaque scoring.

Working definition: what “risk” means (beta)
Risk level is our estimate of the likelihood and severity of negative outcomes if the user applies the suggestion exactly as recommended, assuming their traffic distribution remains similar to the last 7–14 days.
We roll risk up from the following dimensions:
1) Latency risk (p95, p99 deltas; tail amplification)
2) Reliability risk (timeouts, queueing, throttling/backpressure probability)
3) Estimate confidence / data sufficiency (how sure we are about (1) and (2))
4) Operational reversibility / guardrails (can we recommend a safer staged rollout?)

NOTE: We should not claim “quality risk” for batching/caching unless we have concrete evidence. For now, only mention quality in edge cases where caching changes prompt normalization or tool output caching behavior (rare; mostly out of scope for beta).

Principles (copy + product behavior)
- Conservative labeling: when unsure, bump risk UP rather than down (and show “Low confidence” explicitly).
- Tie risk to what the customer cares about: p95/p99 latency and error rate.
- Always pair a risk label with a “how to apply safely” snippet (canary/gradual rollout and rollback instructions).
- Avoid mixing “risk” with “confidence” in one label. Risk is impact/likelihood; confidence is quality of estimate.
- Make it easy for Support/CS to explain. (We will get “why high risk?” questions.)

Proposed risk levels (v0) — user-facing semantics
LOW
- Expected to be safe for most production routes.
- We predict minimal tail-latency impact and no meaningful increase in timeouts.
- Data is sufficient and stable (traffic + latency distributions).

MEDIUM
- Reasonable upside, but more likely to affect tail latency or queueing during peak.
- Recommended only if route has headroom OR user can do a staged rollout.
- Often shows larger variance across time windows.

HIGH
- Material chance of breaking latency SLOs or increasing timeouts under load.
- Usually appears on ultra-low-latency routes, spiky/peaky workloads, or where we have insufficient telemetry / unstable patterns.
- Should require explicit acknowledgment in UI (“Apply anyway” with staged rollout suggested).

We should also have a “Not rated” state
- For cases with insufficient telemetry, misconfigured metrics, or suggestion type requiring missing prerequisites.
- UI should not show a risk badge; show “Insufficient data” instead.

How risk gets computed (high level; intended for internal alignment)
We’re deciding between two things:
A) A simple rules-based mapping (fast to ship, explainable)
B) A numeric score 0–100 mapped to bands (more flexible, risk of opacity)

Current preference for beta: rules-based mapping, with an internal numeric score retained for diagnostics.

Candidate inputs
Latency:
- Baseline p50/p95/p99 over last 7d (or 14d if 7d is sparse)
- Predicted deltas for p50/p95 and “tail multiplier” (p95 delta vs p50 delta)
- Share of requests already near SLA threshold (if customer defines SLO; otherwise use Redwood route defaults)

Reliability / queueing:
- Peak concurrency estimate and burstiness (p95 QPS / median QPS)
- Current queue time contribution (if available) / saturation signals
- Recent timeout rate (baseline) and any correlated spikes

Confidence:
- Telemetry coverage: fraction of traffic instrumented + retention window
- Stability: how much workload changed week-over-week (e.g., seq length distribution drift)
- Model/route eligibility: whether the model/runtime supports the recommended technique equivalently

Guardrail flags (hard overrides)
- If route is tagged “low-latency critical” (or p95 baseline already within X% of target), raise risk.
- If predicted p95 delta exceeds threshold, raise risk regardless of savings.
- If confidence is low, cap at Medium or High (never Low).

Draft thresholds (numbers are placeholders; do not ship without validation)
We need something simple enough for UX + Support but grounded enough for eng to implement.

Latency risk thresholds (for batching suggestions)
- LOW if predicted p95 delta <= +5% AND predicted p50 delta <= +3% AND tail multiplier <= 2x
- MEDIUM if predicted p95 delta is between +5% and +15% OR tail multiplier between 2x and 3x
- HIGH if predicted p95 delta > +15% OR predicted p99 delta > +20% OR tail multiplier > 3x

Latency risk thresholds (for caching suggestions)
- Caching typically improves latency (or neutral), but can introduce cache stampede / memory pressure.
- LOW if cache hit uplift is expected and memory headroom signals are OK; predicted p95 delta <= +3%
- MEDIUM if memory headroom uncertain OR workload burstiness high
- HIGH if burstiness high AND cache warmup/cold-start penalty likely impacts tail (e.g., high cardinality prompts) OR we see OOM/eviction churn indicators

Reliability / timeouts thresholds
- LOW if baseline timeout rate is low and predicted queueing risk is low
- MEDIUM if baseline timeouts exist OR predicted queueing risk increases during peak windows
- HIGH if baseline timeouts are already elevated OR predicted saturation risk is high

Confidence thresholds (separate label; do not blend into risk)
- HIGH confidence: sufficient sample size, stable workload, complete telemetry
- MEDIUM confidence: moderate sample size, minor drift
- LOW confidence: sparse data or high drift; default risk cannot be Low

Open question: should low confidence show as a separate badge?
- Option 1: Add “Confidence: High/Med/Low” as a column + in drawer.
- Option 2: Keep confidence in drawer only, and bump risk when confidence is low.
- Current leaning: Option 1 (explicit), plus “Low confidence” can raise risk one band but not always (avoid making all low-confidence = High).

Proposed user-facing explanations (copy drafts)
We need short tooltip copy + longer drawer copy.

Tooltip copy (table)
- Low risk: “Unlikely to affect latency or reliability for typical production traffic.”
- Medium risk: “May increase tail latency under peak load. Apply with a staged rollout.”
- High risk: “Higher chance of impacting latency SLOs or timeouts. Apply only with careful rollout/rollback.”

Drawer: “Why this risk level?” (bullet templates)
LOW
- “Predicted p95 latency change is small (≤ ~5%) based on the last 7 days of traffic.”
- “Workload is stable (request rate and sequence lengths).”
- “No saturation/timeout signals detected during peak periods.”

MEDIUM
- “Predicted p95 latency may increase (~5–15%), especially during peak concurrency.”
- “Traffic is bursty or shows moderate drift week-over-week.”
- “We recommend a canary rollout and monitoring p95 + timeout rate for 30–60 minutes before expanding.”

HIGH
- “Predicted tail latency increase is significant (> ~15%) or concentrated at peak load.”
- “Route appears latency-sensitive (baseline p95 is close to target) or shows saturation signals.”
- “Apply only if you can roll out gradually and quickly revert.”

Drawer: “How to apply safely” (shared snippet)
- “Start with a small canary (e.g., 1–5% traffic) for at least one peak period.”
- “Monitor: p95/p99 latency, timeout rate, and queue time.”
- “Rollback if p95 increases beyond your SLO budget or if timeout rate rises.”

Alternative label schemes explored (design/PM)
1) Current: Low / Medium / High
Pros: familiar, compact.
Cons: “High risk” can trigger stakeholder anxiety; may be interpreted as security risk.

2) “Safe / Caution / Needs review”
Pros: reduces fear language, more action-oriented.
Cons: “Safe” is too strong; we can’t guarantee.

3) “Low impact / Medium impact / High impact”
Pros: focuses on performance impact rather than “risk.”
Cons: still conflates likelihood vs magnitude; also we already show latency deltas separately.

4) “Recommended / Consider / Advanced”
Pros: more product-y.
Cons: hides the actual risk dimension; “Advanced” not necessarily risk.

5) Dual axis shown as a compact pill: “Risk: Medium • Confidence: Low”
Pros: more honest.
Cons: UI density; needs accessibility review.

Current decision (tentative)
- Keep Low/Medium/High for beta for speed and cross-team alignment.
- Add explicit “Performance & reliability risk” subtitle in tooltip/drawer to disambiguate.
- Add separate confidence indicator in details drawer; consider a table column if space allows.

Examples (for internal sanity checks)
Example A: Batching increase on a non-latency-critical route
- Route: /chat/completions (internal service A)
- Baseline: p50 220ms, p95 680ms; timeouts 0.02%
- Predicted: p50 +2%, p95 +4%; savings $180/day
- Confidence: High (large sample, stable)
=> Risk: LOW
Drawer bullets should emphasize “small tail change” + “stable workload.”

Example B: Batching increase on a latency-sensitive endpoint
- Route: /agent/stream (service B)
- Baseline: p50 95ms, p95 210ms; strict internal SLO p95 < 250ms
- Predicted: p50 +5%, p95 +18% (would push close to/beyond SLO in peak)
- Confidence: Medium
=> Risk: HIGH
Drawer should mention “baseline close to target” + “tail increase concentrated at peak.”

Example C: Caching enablement with uncertain hit rate
- Route: /embeddings (service C)
- Observed prompts high-cardinality; expected cache hit uplift low/uncertain
- Baseline: p95 140ms; no timeouts
- Predicted: p95 +2% median but variance high; savings $60/day (wide band)
- Confidence: Low
=> Risk: MEDIUM (not High) + explicit “Low confidence”
We want to avoid labeling everything High just due to low confidence; better to surface uncertainty.

Example D: Caching suggestion during memory pressure
- Signs of eviction churn / near-capacity GPU memory; elevated p99 spikes
- Predicted: tail latency unstable; risk of OOM/restarts
=> Risk: HIGH
Even if average latency improves, reliability risk dominates.

Edge cases / failure modes we must handle in UX
- “High risk” but large savings: users will still try it. Ensure “How to apply safely” is prominent.
- “Low risk” but low savings: users may ignore; fine.
- “Risk unknown” due to missing telemetry: provide setup CTA, not a misleading label.
- Confusion with compliance/security: add “Performance & reliability” phrasing everywhere risk is mentioned.

Copy warnings we should avoid
- Avoid: “Safe”, “Guaranteed”, “Will not impact latency.”
- Prefer: “Unlikely”, “Based on recent traffic”, “Apply gradually.”

UI/interaction notes (for Design)
- In the table, risk badge should have tooltip with 1–2 sentences.
- In the details drawer, show:
  - Risk level + short definition
  - 2–4 bullets “Why this risk level?” with concrete numbers when possible (p95 delta, confidence note)
  - “How to apply safely” snippet + link to rollout docs/config
- Consider requiring acknowledgement for High risk (checkbox or modal) in later iterations; not required for beta if too heavy.

Open questions / to resolve
1) Do we need “Very High” (4 levels)?
- Concern: current High bucket may be too broad.
- Counter: adds complexity; beta should stay 3-level.

2) Should risk be computed per suggestion or per route?
- Likely per suggestion because same route can have multiple actions with different risk profiles.

3) How to handle partial traffic + mixed models?
- If multiple models behind a route, risk should use weighted traffic distribution.
- If the suggestion is scoped to a specific model variant, explain that in drawer.

4) What does “confidence” mean when we have high sample size but the estimator is known to be biased?
- We may need “Model confidence” (estimator uncertainty) vs “Data confidence” (telemetry sufficiency).
- For beta: merge into one “confidence” and be explicit in caveats.

5) Should we add a “Test in staging” recommendation?
- Might be misleading; staging often doesn’t match traffic distribution. Better: canary in prod.

Next steps
- Align with Console PRD/design spec (Marissa + Tessa/Kenji) on exact label text and tooltip wording.
- Sanity-check thresholds with Applied ML (Maya/Sana) using historical telemetry (see validation plan).
- Confirm guardrail flags with SRE/Platform (Sean Gallagher) to avoid recommending risky batching on low-latency routes.
- Create a short Support explanation template for “Why is this high risk?” (Dev Patel / support readiness).

Changelog (informal)
- 2026-01-19: initial draft (Low/Med/High definitions + alternative label brainstorm)
- 2026-02-02: added confidence separation and copy warnings
- 2026-02-23: added example set + preliminary thresholds; clarified caching-specific risks
